title: Psychodynamic Psychotherapy, Interpersonal Therapy, and Motivational Interviewing

steps.title: Structural Model of the Mind
steps.tx: **Freudian structural model of personality** conceptualizes psychic apparatus as comprising three interactive components: the id, operating entirely in the unconscious on the primal pleasure principle; the ego, governed by the reality principle, mediating between instinctual urges and external society; and the superego, embodying internalized moral conscience and parental prohibitions.

rows: Harbors instinctual sexual (libido) and aggressive drives

steps.tx: Only the tip of this iceberg shows above the waterline, and Freud meant that literally. The conscious ego negotiates at the surface while the **id** churns beneath in the unconscious, pressing pleasure seeking drives against the superego's internalised rules. Psychodynamic therapy listens for how that submerged conflict surfaces as symptoms, dreams and patterns repeated inside the consulting room itself. Whether or not one accepts the whole model, the iceberg remains the quickest sketch of why people act against their own stated intentions.
steps.say: Freud iceberg places the id in the unconscious below an ego and superego negotiating at the surface.

steps.title: Core Psychoanalytic Techniques
steps.tx: **Techniques of classical psychoanalysis** rely upon the fundamental rule of free association, wherein the analysand speaks every spontaneous thought without censorship, allowing unconscious derivatives to surface. The analyst interprets resistance, parapraxes (Freudian slips), and dreams, distinguishing the superficial manifest content from the disguised unconscious latent content shaped by primary process condensation and displacement.

left.title: Manifest Dream Content
points: The literal remembered imagery, storyline, and narrative events consciously recalled by the patient upon awakening

right.title: Latent Dream Content
points: The underlying repressed instinctual wishes, fears, and unacceptable drives disguised by dream work

steps.title: Transference and Countertransference
steps.tx: **Clinical dynamics of transference** occur when a patient unconsciously displaces unresolved feelings, expectations, and conflicts from early significant childhood figures (such as parents) onto the therapist. Conversely, countertransference encompasses the clinician unconscious emotional reactions toward the patient, requiring diligent self-analysis during clinical supervision to prevent boundary blurring or therapeutic distortion.

steps.title: Interpersonal Psychotherapy Domains
steps.tx: **Interpersonal psychotherapy framework** is a time-limited (12 to 16 weeks), empirically validated therapy for major depressive disorder that links mood symptoms to social interactions. IPT focuses exclusively on resolving pathology within four distinct interpersonal problem domains: complicated bereavement and unresolved grief, interpersonal role disputes, stressful role transitions, and pervasive interpersonal social deficits.

steps.title: Dialectical Behaviour Therapy
steps.tx: **Dialectical behaviour therapy for borderline personality** developed by Marsha Linehan balances compassionate radical acceptance of the patient suffering with rigorous commitment to behavioral change. DBT integrates weekly individual psychotherapy, group skills training (mindfulness, interpersonal effectiveness, emotion regulation, distress tolerance), and telephone coaching to eliminate suicidal self-harm and parasuicidal gestures.

steps.tx: Readiness for change is one map, and a specific therapy for borderline personality is another. **Dialectical behaviour therapy for borderline personality**, developed by Marsha Linehan, balances radical acceptance of the patient's suffering with a firm requirement for behavioural change. Treatment combines a weekly individual session, group skills training in mindfulness, interpersonal effectiveness, emotion regulation, and distress tolerance, and telephone coaching between sessions. The practical target is to stop suicidal self harm and parasuicidal gestures.
steps.say: Dialectical behaviour therapy, from Marsha Linehan, accepts the suffering of borderline personality disorder and at the same time insists on behavioural change. Weekly individual therapy, a skills group, and phone coaching aim to stop suicidal and parasuicidal acts. The skills are mindfulness, interpersonal effectiveness, emotion regulation, and distress tolerance.

steps.title: Stages of Change Transtheoretical Model
steps.tx: **Transtheoretical model stages of change** outlines five sequential motivational phases: precontemplation (no intention of modifying behavior within six months), contemplation (recognizing the problem but ambivalently weighing costs and benefits), preparation (intending to take concrete action within thirty days), action (overt behavioral modification), and maintenance (consolidating gains to prevent relapse).

steps.title: Motivational Interviewing Principles
steps.tx: **Core principles of motivational interviewing** provide a client-centered, collaborative counselling style designed to resolve ambivalence regarding substance dependence. Therapists express non-judgmental empathy, develop discrepancy between current substance behaviors and core personal values, roll with interpersonal resistance rather than arguing, and bolster self-efficacy using OARS skills: open questions, affirmations, reflective listening, and summaries.

steps.title: Family Therapy and Expressed Emotion
steps.tx: **Expressed emotion in family dynamics** serves as the strongest psychosocial predictor of relapse in patients with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder following discharge. High expressed emotion comprises three detrimental family behaviors: harsh critical comments, overt hostility, and emotional overinvolvement. Psychoeducational family therapy establishes supportive boundaries, reducing family emotional tension and slashing relapse rates by half.
